fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is adding Ti to CoCrFeNiTi, although Ti is already an equimolar constituent; no additional Ti concentration is specified.
It misses the central intervention of high-energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering.
No quantitative prediction relative to the unmodified alloy is provided.
The stated room-temperature and atmospheric-pressure conditions do not define fabrication conditions and conflict with argon milling and vacuum SPS.
The prediction of increased ductility is unsupported and inconsistent with the target result of high strength but limited ductility/intergranular fracture.
The cited evidence concerns Al addition to FeCoNiCrMn and a general HEA review, so it does not support Ti addition to an alloy already containing Ti.
explanation: The response recognizes the general need to strengthen a low-strength HEA and mentions generic solid-solution/BCC strengthening, but it does not reconstruct the processing hypothesis. It omits milling speed, ball-to-powder ratio, milling duration, SPS temperature, heating rate, and hold time, as well as the nanocrystalline FCC/BCC mediator and porosity suppression. It gives none of the expected quantitative outcomes—approximately 675 HV, 1894 MPa compressive strength, 1238 MPa yield stress, density above 6.5 g/cm³, or 83% FCC/17% BCC. The proposed experiment is only weakly discriminating because it lacks a defined Ti dose, matched processing controls, phase/grain-size criteria, and quantitative falsification thresholds.
